hypothesis: Marine genera that occur in two or more widely separated regions have first and last appearances falling in the same or adjacent geological stage in each region, so that fossil assemblages can be correlated between distant regions.
pass_criterion: Using marine fossil occurrences with stage-level age assignments, take genera with at least 10 occurrences in each of two or more continents, with the continents at least 3000 km apart. For each genus and continent pair, compare the stage of first occurrence (and separately of last occurrence) in each continent. The claim is supported if at least 80% of these comparisons differ by 0 or 1 stage, the median offset is 0 stages, and the share of exact matches is at least twice the share expected when stage labels are shuffled among regions (permutation p < 0.01).
fail_criterion: The claim is refuted if fewer than 60% of comparisons differ by 0 or 1 stage, or if the observed stage offsets are not significantly tighter than the shuffled-label null (permutation p >= 0.05).
interpretation: Darwin's 'forms of life' are marine genera (and species where recorded). 'Change almost simultaneously, in a broad geological sense' means first and last appearances lie within the same or an adjacent International Chronostratigraphic Chart stage (a few Myr), not that they are synchronous to the year. 'Throughout the world' is tested as occurrence on different continents under different palaeoclimates, approximated by PBDB paleolatitude and paleocoordinates. Modern caveat: occurrences are assigned to stages largely using the same fossils, so the dating is partly circular. The test therefore also uses collections with independent age evidence (radiometric or magnetostratigraphic notes) as a robustness subset. Sampling and range-edge effects (the Signor-Lipps effect) widen offsets, so the thresholds allow a one-stage tolerance.

dataset.name: The Paleobiology Database
dataset.why_it_fits: PBDB provides downloadable fossil occurrences and collections through its data service API. Fields that would be used: accepted_name or genus, early_interval, late_interval, max_ma, min_ma, cc (country code), lat/lng, paleolat/paleolng, environment (marine filter) and the collection's geological stage. Together these give per-region first and last appearance stages for the same marine taxa.
